items.evidence_text:
1. Approve a proclamation honoring Commissioner Margaret Gómez for her 
extraordinary service to Travis County. (Judge Brown)

items.evidence_text: 2. Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer

items.evidence_text:
3. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the following: 
    
  A. Outdoor burning in the unincorporated areas of Travis County 
  B. County response to natural disaster or other emergencies, including but 
not limited to necessary measures and actions related to Travis County’s 
response, operations, policies, emergency assistance, agreements, and 
measures necessary to preserve public health and safety and 
rehabilitation of property, and applicable orders, declarations or 
resolutions, and authorization for expenditure of funds and contracts 
related to disaster response and recovery efforts 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider and take appropriate action regarding outdoor burning in unincorporated areas and county emergency response

items.evidence_text:
4. Consider and take appropriate action to approve the Consent by Lien Holder, for 
Travis County Facilities Corporation, a Texas public facility corporation, to grant 
an electric utility easement to the City of Austin, on that property being described 
as 11.58 acres, more or less, consisting of that certain parcel stated to contain 
6.60 acres, more or less, and that certain parcel stated to contain 4.98 acres, 
more or less, being a portion of Outlot 28 and Outlot 31, Division A, Government 
Outlots adjoining the original City of Austin, and being a portion of Lot 1, 
Siegmund Addition, Section Four, a subdivision of Travis County, Texas; and is 
the same property which received legal lot status in City of Austin Case C81-
2026-0137 attached to the Electric Utility Easement, being the same property 
described in that certain Special Warranty Deed recorded in Document No. 
2024130246. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Approve Consent by Lien Holder for Travis County Facilities Corporation to grant electric utility easement to City of Austin

items.evidence_text:
15. Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers and 
discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any 
other necessary budget amendments and transfers attached to Commissioners 
Court backup for the Agenda item: 
    
  A. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a new budget in 
Afterschool Youth Enrichment Fund (0149) of $6,187.50 for revenue 
received by Health and Human Services related to the AmeriCorps 
Formula Grant for the CAPITAL AmeriCorps Project 
  B. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a New Budget of 
$4,300 for Revenue Received from Reliant Energy for the CARE 
Program 
  C. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a new budget in 
the Bluebonnet Electric Fund (2112) of $12,000 for revenue received by 
Health and Human Services related to the Bluebonnet Electric 
Cooperative 
  D. Request from the Travis County Sheriff's Office to add one vehicle to the 
County's fleet which will be purchased from the Office's Inmate Welfare 
Funds 
  E. Request from the Facilities Management Department (FMD) for 
$4,780,050 from a $13,040,000 Capital Improvement Plan Earmark 
against the Capital Acquisition Resources (CAR) Reserve to complete 
work on prioritized projects 
  F. Request from the Technology and Operations Department (TOPS) for a 
total of $703,831 from the Capital Acquisition Resources (CAR) Reserve 
that include $440,565 for the replacement and purchase of Automated 
External Defibrillators (AEDs) across Travis County facilities and the use 
of $263,266 from a $350,000 Earmark Against the CAR Reserve for 
Constable vehicle AEDs with the remaining Earmark of $86,734 to be 
released 
  G. Request from Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) within the Technology 
and Operations Department (TOPS) for $1,756,018 from the Fiscal Year 
2026 Catastrophic Loss Reserve within the Risk Management Fund 
(8955) to cover short-term liabilities for the remainder of the Fiscal Year 
  H. Request from the Juvenile Probation Department to reallocate $416,748 
from the air handler project that was included as part of the Fiscal Year 
2026 Adopted Budget and has a current balance of $534,748. These 
funds will now be used for critical fire panel safety repairs needed in 
Fiscal Year 2026. The Department will request these funds and 
additional funds as part of the Fiscal Year 2027 budget process to 
complete the air handler project 
(Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Consider budget amendments, transfers, and discussion items including HHS, Sheriff, FMD, TOPS, ERM, and Juvenile Probation requests

items.evidence_text: CALL TO ORDER
items.title: Call to Order

items.evidence_text: PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
items.title: Public Communication

items.evidence_text: COUNTY ANNOUNCEMENTS
items.title: County Announcements

items.evidence_text:
1. Approve a proclamation recognizing the week of July 6 - 10, 2026 as Summer 
Learning Week in Travis County. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve proclamation recognizing Summer Learning Week

items.evidence_text: 2. Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer

items.evidence_text:
3. Receive the Travis County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) and 
Popular Annual Financial Report (PAFR) for the fiscal year ended September 
30, 2025. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Receive Travis County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report and Popular Annual Financial Report for FY2025

items.evidence_text:
4. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the following: 
    
  A. Outdoor burning in the unincorporated areas of Travis County 
  B. County response to natural disaster or other emergencies, including but 
not limited to necessary measures and actions related to the disaster or 
emergency, including Travis County’s response, operations, policies, 
emergency assistance, agreements, preparedness for future flood events 
and other disasters, and measures necessary to preserve public health 
and safety and rehabilitation of property, and applicable orders, 
declarations or resolutions, and authorization for expenditure of funds 
and contracts related to disaster response, preparedness and recovery 
efforts 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider action on outdoor burning and county emergency response

items.evidence_text:
5. Consider and take appropriate action to approve a second budget revision 
request from a Supportive Housing Subrecipient, Mobile Loaves & Fishes, 
reflected in the Subaward for Affordable Housing for the Homeless, Contract No. 
4400006882. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Approve second budget revision for Mobile Loaves & Fishes supportive housing subaward

items.evidence_text:
6. Consider and take appropriate action on the following grant Letters of Intent, 
contracts and related special budgets, and permissions to continue: 
    
  A. Application from the Travis County Juvenile Probation Department for the 
2027 Restorative Justice and Victim Services Program solicited by the 
Texas Bar Foundation 
  B. Application from the Travis County Juvenile Probation Department for the 
2027-2028 Discretionary State Aid Residential Projects solicited by the 
Texas Juvenile Justice Department 
  C. Amendment from Travis County Health and Human Services for the 
AmeriCorps Seniors Programs Grant Agreement  
  D. Award agreement from the Corporation for National and Community 
Services for the AmeriCorps Retired and Senior Volunteer Program 
within Health & Human Services 
  E. Any other necessary grant applications, letters of support or grant awards 
attached to Commissioners Court backup for this Agenda item 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider grant Letters of Intent, contracts, and related special budgets

items.evidence_text:
7. Consider and take appropriate action on a comment letter for proposed changes 
to the Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance (docket OMB-2026-0034). 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider comment letter on proposed changes to Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance

items.evidence_text:
8. Lease Agreement with Austin Ridge Bible Church for Travis County Sheriff's 
Office COBRA Graduation Ceremonies. (Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Lease Agreement with Austin Ridge Bible Church for TCSO COBRA Graduation Ceremonies

items.evidence_text: 9. Authorize the County Treasurer to invest County funds. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Authorize County Treasurer to invest County funds

items.evidence_text:
10. Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers and 
discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any 
other necessary budget amendments and transfers attached to Commissioners 
Court backup for the Agenda item: 
    
  A. Request from Health and Human Services to Establish a New Budget of 
$17,288.20 comprised of $4,769.10 in Fund 2034 for the Texas Gas 
Service – Share the Warmth Program and $12,519.10 in Fund 2112 for 
the Bluebonnet Electric Cooperative 
  B. Request from Transportation and Natural Resources to use up to $2,860 
of existing internal departmental resources to purchase food/beverages 
for the 3rd Annual Road and Bridge Equipment Rodeo and Annual 
Department-Wide TNR Safety and Employee Recognition Event 
  C. Request from the County Clerk’s Office to internally fund the creation of 
an Elections Administrator Assistant (1.0 FTE) to address increased 
workload within the Elections Division at a cost of $58,804 for the 
remainder of Fiscal Year 2026, with the full year annualized cost of 
$152,546 that will be funded within existing resources in the Fiscal Year 
2027 Preliminary Budget 
  D. Request from the Planning and Budget Office for $25,000 from the 
Allocated Reserve to fund an update to the analysis related to the 
collection of venue tax under Chapter 334 related to Travis County 
Exposition Center 
(Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Consider budget amendments, transfers, and discussion items

items.evidence_text:
11. Consider and take appropriate action on a request from the Visit Austin for the 
County to act as the Endorsing County for and to appoint the Austin Sports 
Commission as its exclusive designee and Local Organizing Committee for an 
application to participate in the Texas Events Trust Fund with respect to the 
2026 Good Good Golf Championship to be held at the grounds and facilities of 
the Omni Barton Creek Resort and Spa, Fazio Canyons Course, in Travis 
County on November 9-15, 2026. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider action on Visit Austin request for Texas Events Trust Fund application for Good Good Golf Championship

items.evidence_text:
12. Consider and take appropriate action on a resolution approving and authorizing 
a financing agreement for the Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District. (This 
item will be taken into executive session under the Consultation with Attorney 
exception, Texas Government Code §551.071) (Commissioner Travillion).
items.title: Resolution approving financing agreement for Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District (executive session)

items.evidence_text: 13. Receive bids from County Purchasing Agent. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Receive bids from County Purchasing Agent

items.evidence_text:
14. Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007201 with Square One 
Consultants, Inc., in the deductive amount of $461,094.00, for Supportive 
Housing Construction Compliance and Monitoring Services. (Health and Human 
Services) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007201 with Square One Consultants, Inc. for Supportive Housing Construction Compliance and Monitoring Services

items.evidence_text:
15. Approve contract award for consulting services for U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service 
(USFWS) Regional Permit and Balcones Canyonlands Conservation Plan 
(BCCP), RFS No. 145-JH, in the amount of $2,048,982.00, to the highest-
ranked respondent, ICF Environmental, Inc. (Transportation & Natural 
Resources) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve contract award for consulting services for USFWS Regional Permit and BCCP, RFS No. 145-JH

items.evidence_text:
16. Declare items surplus property and sell at public auction pursuant to Local 
Government Code, Section 263.152(a)(1). (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Declare items surplus property and sell at public auction

items.evidence_text:
17. Approve Modification No. 9 to Contract No. 4400006451 with Alliant Insurance 
Services, Inc., in the amount of $128,075.93, for cyber security insurance broker 
of record services. (Technology & Operations) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 9 to Contract No. 4400006451 with Alliant Insurance Services, Inc. for cyber security insurance broker services

items.evidence_text:
18. Approve Modification No. 2 to Contract No. 4400007807 with Mend 
Collaborative, Inc., in the amount of $70,500.00, for the Travis County Parks 
Comprehensive Plan. (Transportation and Natural Resources) (Commissioner 
Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 2 to Contract No. 4400007807 with Mend Collaborative, Inc. for Travis County Parks Comprehensive Plan

items.evidence_text:
19. Approve Modification No. 11 to Contract 4400001439 with Medicalistics, LLC., in 
the amount of $10,980.00, for Electronic Medical Records Software and 
Maintenance. (TCSO) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 11 to Contract 4400001439 with Medicalistics, LLC for Electronic Medical Records Software and Maintenance

items.evidence_text:
20. Reject all proposals received for RFP No. 129-LC, for Accounting Software. (Tax 
Office) (Commissioners Travillion)
items.title: Reject all proposals for RFP No. 129-LC for Accounting Software

items.evidence_text:
21. Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007202 with Guidehouse, Inc., 
in the deductive amount of $614,252.00, for Supportive Housing Construction 
Compliance and Monitoring Services. (Health and Human Services) 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007202 with Guidehouse, Inc. for Supportive Housing Construction Compliance and Monitoring Services

items.evidence_text:
22. Consider and take appropriate action on the following Personnel Amendments: 
    
  A. Routine Personnel Actions 
  B. Non-Routine Personnel Actions 
(Commissioners Travillion & Morales)
items.title: Consider Personnel Amendments (Routine and Non-Routine)

items.evidence_text:
23. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the approval of the license 
agreement between Travis County and Great Promise for American Indians to 
use a portion of the grounds at the Exposition Center on November 20 and 21, 
2026 for Austin Powwow and Native Market, waiving the related facility rental 
fees. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider license agreement with Great Promise for American Indians for Austin Powwow at Exposition Center

items.evidence_text:
24. Consider and take appropriate action on the Construction and Traffic Mitigation 
Agreement between Lund Farm Investment LLC, a Texas limited liability 
company, and Travis County, for traffic mitigation associated with the proposed 
Lund Road Farms Development, in Precinct One. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Consider Construction and Traffic Mitigation Agreement with Lund Farm Investment LLC for Lund Road Farms Development

items.evidence_text:
25. Consider and take appropriate action on a Subdivision Construction Agreement 
between Sunfield Investments LLC, Sunfield Municipal Utility District No.2, and 
Travis County for the construction of street and drainage improvements for 
Bright Light Boulevard Segment 3, a proposed subdivision, in Precinct Four. 
(Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Consider Subdivision Construction Agreement for Bright Light Boulevard Segment 3

items.evidence_text:
26. Consider and take appropriate action on a Subdivision Construction Agreement 
between Sunfield Investments LLC, Sunfield Municipal Utility District No.3, and 
Travis County for the construction of street and drainage improvements for 
Bright Light Boulevard Segment 2, a proposed subdivision, in Precinct Four. 
(Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Consider Subdivision Construction Agreement for Bright Light Boulevard Segment 2

items.evidence_text:
27. Approve the minutes for the May 5, May 12, and May 19, 2026, Voting 
Sessions. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve minutes for May 5, May 12, and May 19, 2026 Voting Sessions

items.evidence_text:
28. Receive briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County security 
and information security issues.1,4 & 6 (Commissioner Travillion & Howard)
items.title: Executive Session: Receive briefing on Travis County security and information security issues

items.evidence_text:
29. Receive legal briefing and take appropriate action regarding Cause No. D-1-GN-
25-009885, Shane Saum and Jeffery Bowen vs. The Travis County 
Commissioners Court, Andy Brown, Jeffrey Travillion, Brigid Shea, Ann Howard, 
and Margaret Gomez, All in Their Official Capacities; In the 98th Judicial District 
Court, Travis County, Texas.1 (Judge Brown)
items.title: Executive Session: Receive legal briefing on Cause No. D-1-GN-25-009885, Shane Saum and Jeffery Bowen vs. Travis County Commissioners Court

items.evidence_text:
30. Receive legal briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County 
Supportive Housing Initiative related to ANE Webberville, LLC, Contract No. 
4400007226.1 (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Executive Session: Receive legal briefing on Travis County Supportive Housing Initiative related to ANE Webberville, LLC

items.evidence_text: ADJOURN
items.title: Adjourn Commissioners Court Voting Session

items.evidence_text:
1. Consider and take appropriate action on a resolution approving and authorizing 
a financing agreement for the Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District. 
(Commissioner Traviilion)
items.title: Travis County Development Authority: Consider resolution approving financing agreement for Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District

items.title: Adjourn Travis County Development Authority Voting Session

discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any

budget of $77,500 in the General Fund (0001) for Tree Mitigation Fees

4.
CONSENT AGENDA
Each of these items is recommended by the Staff and approval thereof will be strictly on the basis of the Staff recommendations.  Approval of the Consent Agenda authorizes the City Manager or his designee to implement each item in accordance with the Staff recommendations.  The City Council has received background information and has had an opportunity to raise questions regarding these items prior to consideration.  Citizens may speak on items listed on the Consent Agenda.  A Request to Speak Card should be completed and returned to the City Secretary before Council considers the Consent Agenda.  Citizen comments on Consent Agenda items are limited to three minutes.
Listed below are bids, purchase orders, contracts, and other items to be approved under the Consent Agenda (Agenda Items A - GG).  This listing is provided on the Consent Agenda to allow Council Members to discuss or withdraw an item prior to approval of the Consent Agenda.  If no items are pulled, Consent Agenda Items A - GG below will be approved with one motion.  If items are pulled for separate discussion, they may be considered as the first items following approval of the Consent Agenda.
A.

3.
Hold a discussion on complementary amendments to the Denton Development Code, specifically Subchapters 5, 7, 16, and 22, relating to Gas Well Drilling and Production, Definitions, and Procedures, in light of City Council’s action to remand DCA14-0009 back to the Planning and Zoning Commission after the Governor signed House Bill 40 into law on May 18, 2015. (Darren Groth)
items.title: Work Session: Discussion on complementary DDC amendments for gas well drilling (Subchapters 5, 7, 16, 22) after HB 40 remand

items.evidence_text:
A.
Consult with and provide direction to City’s attorneys regarding legal issues and strategies associated with the current Gas Well Ordinance, and proposed Gas Well Ordinance amendment, regulation of gas well drilling and production within the City Limits and the extraterritorial jurisdiction, including: Constitutional limitations, statutory limitations upon municipal regulatory authority; statutory preemption and vested rights; impacts of federal and state law and regulations; impacts of gas well drilling upon protected uses and vice-versa; current and proposed extension to moratorium on drilling and production; other concerns about municipal regulatory authority or matters relating to enforcement of the Gas Well Ordinance, both current and proposed; settlement matters concerning gas well drilling in the City; surface development issues involving surface and mineral estates; and legal matters associated with a citizen’s initiative ordinance and pending litigation styled George P. Bush, Commissioner, Texas General Land Office v. City of Denton Texas, Cause No. 15-02058-362 currently pending in the 362nd District Court of Denton County and Texas Oil and Gas Association v. City of Denton, Cause No. 14-08933-431 currently pending in the 431st District Court of Denton County regarding hydraulic fracturing where a public discussion of these legal matters would conflict with the duty of the City’s attorneys under the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct of the State Bar of Texas.
items.title: Closed Meeting: Consultation with attorneys on gas well ordinance legal issues and pending litigation

EXECUTIVE SESSION (No public discussion) 
The Zoning & Platting Commission will announce it will go into Executive Session, if necessary, 
pursuant to Chapter 551 of the Texas Government Code, to receive advice from Legal Counsel on

15. Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers and 
discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any 
other necessary budget amendments and transfers attached to Commissioners 
Court backup for the Agenda item: 
    
  A. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a new budget in 
Afterschool Youth Enrichment Fund (0149) of $6,187.50 for revenue 
received by Health and Human Services related to the AmeriCorps 
Formula Grant for the CAPITAL AmeriCorps Project 
  B. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a New Budget of 
$4,300 for Revenue Received from Reliant Energy for the CARE 
Program 
  C. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a new budget in 
the Bluebonnet Electric Fund (2112) of $12,000 for revenue received by 
Health and Human Services related to the Bluebonnet Electric 
Cooperative 
  D. Request from the Travis County Sheriff's Office to add one vehicle to the 
County's fleet which will be purchased from the Office's Inmate Welfare 
Funds 
  E. Request from the Facilities Management Department (FMD) for 
$4,780,050 from a $13,040,000 Capital Improvement Plan Earmark 
against the Capital Acquisition Resources (CAR) Reserve to complete 
work on prioritized projects 
  F. Request from the Technology and Operations Department (TOPS) for a 
total of $703,831 from the Capital Acquisition Resources (CAR) Reserve 
that include $440,565 for the replacement and purchase of Automated 
External Defibrillators (AEDs) across Travis County facilities and the use 
of $263,266 from a $350,000 Earmark Against the CAR Reserve for 
Constable vehicle AEDs with the remaining Earmark of $86,734 to be 
released 
  G. Request from Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) within the Technology 
and Operations Department (TOPS) for $1,756,018 from the Fiscal Year 
2026 Catastrophic Loss Reserve within the Risk Management Fund 
(8955) to cover short-term liabilities for the remainder of the Fiscal Year 
  H. Request from the Juvenile Probation Department to reallocate $416,748 
from the air handler project that was included as part of the Fiscal Year 
2026 Adopted Budget and has a current balance of $534,748. These 
funds will now be used for critical fire panel safety repairs needed in 
Fiscal Year 2026. The Department will request these funds and 
additional funds as part of the Fiscal Year 2027 budget process to 
complete the air handler project 
(Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Act on budget amendments, transfers, and discussion items

items.evidence_text: CALL TO ORDER
items.title: Call to order

items.evidence_text:
1. Approve a proclamation recognizing the week of July 6 - 10, 2026 as Summer 
Learning Week in Travis County. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve proclamation recognizing Summer Learning Week (July 6 - 10, 2026) in Travis County

items.evidence_text: 2. Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer

items.evidence_text:
3. Receive the Travis County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) and 
Popular Annual Financial Report (PAFR) for the fiscal year ended September 
30, 2025. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Receive Travis County ACFR and PAFR for fiscal year ended September 30, 2025

items.evidence_text:
4. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the following: 
    
  A. Outdoor burning in the unincorporated areas of Travis County 
  B. County response to natural disaster or other emergencies, including but 
not limited to necessary measures and actions related to the disaster or 
emergency, including Travis County’s response, operations, policies, 
emergency assistance, agreements, preparedness for future flood events 
and other disasters, and measures necessary to preserve public health 
and safety and rehabilitation of property, and applicable orders, 
declarations or resolutions, and authorization for expenditure of funds 
and contracts related to disaster response, preparedness and recovery 
efforts 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider action on outdoor burning and county disaster/emergency response

items.evidence_text:
5. Consider and take appropriate action to approve a second budget revision 
request from a Supportive Housing Subrecipient, Mobile Loaves & Fishes, 
reflected in the Subaward for Affordable Housing for the Homeless, Contract No. 
4400006882. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Approve second budget revision request from Mobile Loaves & Fishes (Contract No. 4400006882)

items.evidence_text:
6. Consider and take appropriate action on the following grant Letters of Intent, 
contracts and related special budgets, and permissions to continue: 
    
  A. Application from the Travis County Juvenile Probation Department for the 
2027 Restorative Justice and Victim Services Program solicited by the 
Texas Bar Foundation 
  B. Application from the Travis County Juvenile Probation Department for the 
2027-2028 Discretionary State Aid Residential Projects solicited by the 
Texas Juvenile Justice Department 
  C. Amendment from Travis County Health and Human Services for the 
AmeriCorps Seniors Programs Grant Agreement  
  D. Award agreement from the Corporation for National and Community 
Services for the AmeriCorps Retired and Senior Volunteer Program 
within Health & Human Services 
  E. Any other necessary grant applications, letters of support or grant awards 
attached to Commissioners Court backup for this Agenda item 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider action on grant letters of intent, contracts, special budgets, and permissions to continue

items.evidence_text:
7. Consider and take appropriate action on a comment letter for proposed changes 
to the Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance (docket OMB-2026-0034). 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve comment letter on proposed changes to Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance (OMB-2026-0034)

items.evidence_text:
8. Lease Agreement with Austin Ridge Bible Church for Travis County Sheriff's 
Office COBRA Graduation Ceremonies. (Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Approve lease agreement with Austin Ridge Bible Church for Sheriff's Office COBRA graduation ceremonies

items.evidence_text: 9. Authorize the County Treasurer to invest County funds. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Authorize County Treasurer to invest County funds

items.evidence_text:
11. Consider and take appropriate action on a request from the Visit Austin for the 
County to act as the Endorsing County for and to appoint the Austin Sports 
Commission as its exclusive designee and Local Organizing Committee for an 
application to participate in the Texas Events Trust Fund with respect to the 
2026 Good Good Golf Championship to be held at the grounds and facilities of 
the Omni Barton Creek Resort and Spa, Fazio Canyons Course, in Travis 
County on November 9-15, 2026. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Act as Endorsing County and appoint Austin Sports Commission for Texas Events Trust Fund application (2026 Good Good Golf Championship)

items.evidence_text:
12. Consider and take appropriate action on a resolution approving and authorizing 
a financing agreement for the Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District. (This 
item will be taken into executive session under the Consultation with Attorney 
exception, Texas Government Code §551.071) (Commissioner Travillion).
items.title: Approve resolution authorizing financing agreement for Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District

items.evidence_text: 13. Receive bids from County Purchasing Agent. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Receive bids from County Purchasing Agent

items.evidence_text:
14. Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007201 with Square One 
Consultants, Inc., in the deductive amount of $461,094.00, for Supportive 
Housing Construction Compliance and Monitoring Services. (Health and Human 
Services) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007201 with Square One Consultants (deductive $461,094.00)

items.evidence_text:
15. Approve contract award for consulting services for U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service 
(USFWS) Regional Permit and Balcones Canyonlands Conservation Plan 
(BCCP), RFS No. 145-JH, in the amount of $2,048,982.00, to the highest-
ranked respondent, ICF Environmental, Inc. (Transportation & Natural 
Resources) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve contract award to ICF Environmental for USFWS Regional Permit/BCCP consulting ($2,048,982.00)

items.evidence_text:
16. Declare items surplus property and sell at public auction pursuant to Local 
Government Code, Section 263.152(a)(1). (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Declare surplus property and sell at public auction under Local Government Code 263.152(a)(1)

items.evidence_text:
17. Approve Modification No. 9 to Contract No. 4400006451 with Alliant Insurance 
Services, Inc., in the amount of $128,075.93, for cyber security insurance broker 
of record services. (Technology & Operations) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 9 to Contract No. 4400006451 with Alliant Insurance ($128,075.93)

items.evidence_text:
18. Approve Modification No. 2 to Contract No. 4400007807 with Mend 
Collaborative, Inc., in the amount of $70,500.00, for the Travis County Parks 
Comprehensive Plan. (Transportation and Natural Resources) (Commissioner 
Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 2 to Contract No. 4400007807 with Mend Collaborative ($70,500.00)

items.evidence_text:
19. Approve Modification No. 11 to Contract 4400001439 with Medicalistics, LLC., in 
the amount of $10,980.00, for Electronic Medical Records Software and 
Maintenance. (TCSO) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 11 to Contract 4400001439 with Medicalistics ($10,980.00)

items.evidence_text:
20. Reject all proposals received for RFP No. 129-LC, for Accounting Software. (Tax 
Office) (Commissioners Travillion)
items.title: Reject all proposals for RFP No. 129-LC (Accounting Software)

items.evidence_text:
21. Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007202 with Guidehouse, Inc., 
in the deductive amount of $614,252.00, for Supportive Housing Construction 
Compliance and Monitoring Services. (Health and Human Services) 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007202 with Guidehouse (deductive $614,252.00)

items.evidence_text:
22. Consider and take appropriate action on the following Personnel Amendments: 
    
  A. Routine Personnel Actions 
  B. Non-Routine Personnel Actions 
(Commissioners Travillion & Morales)
items.title: Consider personnel amendments: routine and non-routine personnel actions

items.evidence_text:
23. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the approval of the license 
agreement between Travis County and Great Promise for American Indians to 
use a portion of the grounds at the Exposition Center on November 20 and 21, 
2026 for Austin Powwow and Native Market, waiving the related facility rental 
fees. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve license agreement with Great Promise for American Indians for Austin Powwow and Native Market, waiving rental fees

items.evidence_text:
24. Consider and take appropriate action on the Construction and Traffic Mitigation 
Agreement between Lund Farm Investment LLC, a Texas limited liability 
company, and Travis County, for traffic mitigation associated with the proposed 
Lund Road Farms Development, in Precinct One. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Construction and Traffic Mitigation Agreement with Lund Farm Investment LLC (Lund Road Farms, Precinct One)

items.evidence_text:
25. Consider and take appropriate action on a Subdivision Construction Agreement 
between Sunfield Investments LLC, Sunfield Municipal Utility District No.2, and 
Travis County for the construction of street and drainage improvements for 
Bright Light Boulevard Segment 3, a proposed subdivision, in Precinct Four. 
(Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Approve Subdivision Construction Agreement for Bright Light Boulevard Segment 3 with Sunfield Investments/Sunfield MUD No. 2 (Precinct Four)

items.evidence_text:
26. Consider and take appropriate action on a Subdivision Construction Agreement 
between Sunfield Investments LLC, Sunfield Municipal Utility District No.3, and 
Travis County for the construction of street and drainage improvements for 
Bright Light Boulevard Segment 2, a proposed subdivision, in Precinct Four. 
(Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Approve Subdivision Construction Agreement for Bright Light Boulevard Segment 2 with Sunfield Investments/Sunfield MUD No. 3 (Precinct Four)

items.evidence_text:
27. Approve the minutes for the May 5, May 12, and May 19, 2026, Voting 
Sessions. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve minutes for May 5, May 12, and May 19, 2026 voting sessions

items.evidence_text:
28. Receive briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County security 
and information security issues.1,4 & 6 (Commissioner Travillion & Howard)
items.title: Receive briefing on Travis County security and information security issues

items.evidence_text:
29. Receive legal briefing and take appropriate action regarding Cause No. D-1-GN-
25-009885, Shane Saum and Jeffery Bowen vs. The Travis County 
Commissioners Court, Andy Brown, Jeffrey Travillion, Brigid Shea, Ann Howard, 
and Margaret Gomez, All in Their Official Capacities; In the 98th Judicial District 
Court, Travis County, Texas.1 (Judge Brown)
items.title: Receive legal briefing on Shane Saum and Jeffery Bowen v. Travis County Commissioners Court (Cause No. D-1-GN-25-009885)

items.evidence_text:
30. Receive legal briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County 
Supportive Housing Initiative related to ANE Webberville, LLC, Contract No. 
4400007226.1 (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Receive legal briefing on Supportive Housing Initiative related to ANE Webberville LLC (Contract No. 4400007226)

items.evidence_text: ADJOURN
items.title: Adjourn Commissioners Court voting session

items.evidence_text: ADJOURN
items.title: Adjourn Travis County Development Authority voting session

items.evidence_text:
10. Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers and 
discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any 
other necessary budget amendments and transfers attached to Commissioners 
Court backup for the Agenda item: 
    
  A. Request from Health and Human Services to Establish a New Budget of 
$17,288.20 comprised of $4,769.10 in Fund 2034 for the Texas Gas 
Service – Share the Warmth Program and $12,519.10 in Fund 2112 for 
the Bluebonnet Electric Cooperative 
  B. Request from Transportation and Natural Resources to use up to $2,860 
of existing internal departmental resources to purchase food/beverages 
for the 3rd Annual Road and Bridge Equipment Rodeo and Annual 
Department-Wide TNR Safety and Employee Recognition Event 
  C. Request from the County Clerk’s Office to internally fund the creation of 
an Elections Administrator Assistant (1.0 FTE) to address increased 
workload within the Elections Division at a cost of $58,804 for the 
remainder of Fiscal Year 2026, with the full year annualized cost of 
$152,546 that will be funded within existing resources in the Fiscal Year 
2027 Preliminary Budget 
  D. Request from the Planning and Budget Office for $25,000 from the 
Allocated Reserve to fund an update to the analysis related to the 
collection of venue tax under Chapter 334 related to Travis County 
Exposition Center 
(Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Consider action on budget amendments, transfers, and discussion items

1. Consider and take appropriate action on a resolution approving and authorizing 
a financing agreement for the Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District. 
(Commissioner Traviilion)
items.title: Approve resolution authorizing financing agreement for Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District

4.
CONSENT AGENDA
Each of these items is recommended by the Staff and approval thereof will be strictly on the basis of the Staff recommendations.  Approval of the Consent Agenda authorizes the City Manager or his designee to implement each item in accordance with the Staff recommendations.  The City Council has received background information and has had an opportunity to raise questions regarding these items prior to consideration.  Citizens may speak on items listed on the Consent Agenda.  A Request to Speak Card should be completed and returned to the City Secretary before Council considers the Consent Agenda.  Citizen comments on Consent Agenda items are limited to three minutes.
Listed below are bids, purchase orders, contracts, and other items to be approved under the Consent Agenda (Agenda Items A - GG).  This listing is provided on the Consent Agenda to allow Council Members to discuss or withdraw an item prior to approval of the Consent Agenda.  If no items are pulled, Consent Agenda Items A - GG below will be approved with one motion.  If items are pulled for separate discussion, they may be considered as the first items following approval of the Consent Agenda.
items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A–GG)

A.

items.title: Resolution approving naming of Center for the Visual Arts after Fred and Patsy Patterson and Roy Appleton, Jr.

items.evidence_text:
B.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City Council of the City of Denton authorizing the City Manager to approve a Settlement Agreement by and between the City of Denton, Texas and EagleRidge Energy, LLC and EagleRidge Operating, LLC relating to locations allowed for gas well drilling in the city, limitations on drilling, operational requirements, gas well site plans, gas well permits, vested rights, and other matters involving EagleRidge’s gas well operations in the city; and further approving a Specific Use Permit to allow gas well drilling and production on a property located within a Neighborhood Residential Mixed Use (NRMU) zoning and use district on approximately 2.64 acres generally located south of Airport Road, east of Interstate 35 West, and west of South Bonnie Brae Street (S09-0007) and as to the Specific Use Permit approval, providing for a penalty in the maximum amount of $2,000.00 for violations thereof; providing for severability and effective dates.
items.title: Ordinance authorizing Settlement Agreement with EagleRidge and SUP for gas well drilling

items.evidence_text:
C.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas approving a second amendment to an Economic Development Program Grant Agreement dated June 15, 2010, between the City of Denton and Allegiance Hillview, L.P., which was duly assigned, in part, to RED Rayzor Ranch, LLC; and providing an effective date.
items.title: Ordinance approving second amendment to Economic Development Program Grant Agreement with Allegiance Hillview/RED Rayzor Ranch

items.evidence_text:
D.
Consider approval of a resolution accepting a petition to annex 40.33 acres of land contiguous to the City of Denton, Texas, located in the northeastern area of the City of Denton’s Extraterritorial Jurisdiction (ETJ); generally located northeast of the City limits, on the west side of Cooper Creek Road approximately 1,200 feet north of Fishtrap Road and 800 feet south of Silver Dome Road and legally described as being a tract of land situated in the Thomas H. Living Survey, Abstract No. 729, Denton County, Texas and being all of a tract of land described in the deed to C.L. Byrom and wife, Anita Byrom as recorded in Volume 308 Page 264 of the deed records of Denton County, Texas. (A14-0001, Windsor Oaks)
items.title: Resolution accepting petition to annex 40.33 acres (Windsor Oaks)

items.evidence_text:
E.
Consider an appeal of the denial of a Certificate of Appropriateness by the Historic Landmark Commission to accept previously installed windows, flagstone on the floor of the front porch and a wood fence on the northeastern side of the property.  The request also included approval of existing paint on the window trim, chimney of the house, and new construction of a driveway gate on the southeastern side of the house.  The property is located at 1807 N. Bell Avenue and is within a Neighborhood Residential 3 (NR-3) zoning district and the Bell Avenue Historic Conservation District. On April 14, 2014, the Historic Landmark Commission denied the request (8-0).
items.title: Appeal of denial of Certificate of Appropriateness (1807 N. Bell Avenue)

items.evidence_text:
A.
Hold a public hearing and consider approval of a resolution of the City Council of Denton, Texas, making findings that the proposed Rayzor Ranch Public Improvement District No. 1 and the proposed public improvements will promote the interests of the City and confer a special benefit on a definable part of the City; providing that the district and proposed public improvements are feasible and advisable; providing findings with respect to the nature and estimated cost of the proposed public improvements, the boundaries of the district, the method of assessment, and apportionment of costs between the District and the City; authorizing the creation of the District and directing the City Secretary or other officer to publish notice of the creation; and providing an effective date.  The Economic Development Partnership Board recommends approval (7-0).
items.title: Public hearing: Resolution creating Rayzor Ranch Public Improvement District No. 1

items.evidence_text:
C.
Hold a public hearing and consider adoption of an ordinance regarding a Specific Use Permit (SUP) to allow construction of a wet weather pump station and detention facility use on a property located in a Neighborhood Residential 2 (NR-2) zoning and use district on approximately 65.94 acres.  The subject property is generally located west of Country Club Road and KCS Railroad, east of Fort Worth Drive, and south of Bent Creek Estate Residential Subdivision; and providing for a penalty in the maximum amount of $2,000.00 for violations, thereof, severability and an effective date. (S14-0002, Hickory Creek Detention Facility) The Planning and Zoning Commission recommends approval (7-0).
items.title: Public hearing: Ordinance regarding SUP for wet weather pump station (S14-0002)

items.evidence_text:
D.
Hold a public hearing and consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas, denying a request for an Environmentally Sensitive Area Alternative Development Plan on approximately 3.71 acres of land, generally located at the northeast corner of E. University Drive (U.S. 380) and Loop 288, within a Employment Center Industrial (EC-I) zoning district and legally described as within the W. Lloyd Survey, Abstract Number 774, in the City of Denton, Denton County, Texas; providing for a penalty in the maximum amount of $2,000.00 for violations thereof; providing a severability clause and an effective date. (ADP13-0004) The Planning and Zoning Commission recommended denial of this request (4-3).  A SUPERMAJORITY VOTE BY COUNCIL IS REQUIRED FOR APPROVAL.
items.title: Public hearing: Ordinance denying Environmentally Sensitive Area Alternative Development Plan (ADP13-0004)

items.evidence_text:
A.
Under Section 551.042 of the Texas Open Meetings Act, respond to inquiries from the City Council or the public with specific factual information or recitation of policy, or accept a proposal to place the matter on the agenda for an upcoming meeting  AND  Under Section 551.0415 of the Texas Open Meetings Act, provide reports about items of community interest regarding which no action will be taken, to include: expressions of thanks, congratulations, or condolence; information regarding holiday schedules; an honorary or salutary recognition of a public official, public employee, or other citizen; a reminder about an upcoming event organized or sponsored by the governing body; information regarding a social, ceremonial, or community event organized or sponsored by an entity other than the governing body that was attended or is scheduled to be attended by a member of the governing body or an official or employee of the municipality; or an announcement involving an imminent threat to the public health and safety of people in the municipality that has arisen after the posting of the agenda.
items.title: Respond to inquiries and provide reports about items of community interest

items.evidence_text:
B.
Possible Continuation of Closed Meeting under Sections 551.071-551.086 of the Texas Open Meetings Act.
items.title: Possible Continuation of Closed Meeting

items.evidence_text:
B.
Certain Public Power Utilities: Competitive Matters - Under Texas Government Code Section 551.086.
1.
Receive a briefing and information pertaining to certain competitive public power and financial issues regarding Texas Municipal Power Agency ("TMPA") on matters including, without limitation: present and future plant operations issues, plant and system expenses, maintenance issues, performance issues, financial issues, reliability issues, planning issues, and any related issues concerning the City’s interest in, and its business relationship with the Texas Municipal Power Agency; and discuss, deliberate, and provide Staff with direction regarding such matters. (Bunselmeyer)
items.title: Closed Meeting: Competitive public power matters regarding TMPA

items.evidence_text:
C.
Certain Public Power Utilities: Competitive Matters - Under Texas Government Code Section 551.086; and Consultation with Attorneys - Under Texas Government Code Section 551.071.
1.
Receive competitive public power, financial and commercial information from Denton Municipal Electric ("DME") staff regarding the acquisition, integration and implementation of ERCOT Shadow Settlement Software in its Energy Management Division relating to its power purchase operations, which includes bidding and pricing information for purchased power, generation and fuel, and Electric Reliability Council of Texas bids, prices, offers, and related services for purposes of supporting the Energy Management Division of DME; discuss, deliberate, provide staff with direction, consider and take final action.  Consultation with the City’s attorneys regarding legal issues associated with the above acquisition where a public discussion of these legal matters would conflict with the duty of the City’s attorneys to the City of Denton and the Denton City Council under the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct of the State Bar of Texas, or would jeopardize the City’s legal position in any administrative proceeding or potential litigation. (Michael Copeland)
items.title: Closed Meeting: DME ERCOT Shadow Settlement Software acquisition and legal consultation

items.evidence_text:
A.
Consider adoption of an ordinance finding that a public use and necessity exists to acquire through the exercise of the right of eminent domain (I) fee simple to a 7.393 acre tract (the "Mayhill Tract"); (II) fee simple to a 4.508 acre tract (the "Landfill Tract"); and (III) a Slope Easement (herein so called), encumbering a 0.804 acre tract, each affected tract located in the John B. Brandon Survey, Abstract Number 1515, City of Denton, Denton County, Texas, as more particularly described on Exhibit "A", attached hereto and made a part hereof, located generally in the 1400 block of South Mayhill Road (the "Property Interests"), for (A) as concerns the Mayhill tract and the Slope Easement, the public use of expanding and improving Mayhill Road, a municipal street and roadway; and (B) as concerns the Landfill Tract, for the public use of expanding and improving the City of Denton Landfill, a permitted municipal Solid Waste disposal facility; authorizing the filing and prosecution of eminent domain proceedings to acquire the Property Interest; authorizing the expenditure of funds therefore: making findings; providing a savings clause; and providing an effective date.  (Parcel 134 RTS&M, LLC- Mayhill Road Widening and Improvements project and City of Denton Landfill, a permitted municipal solid waste disposal facility)
items.title: Eminent domain consideration for Mayhill Tract, Landfill Tract, and Slope Easement

items.evidence_text:
B.
Hold a public hearing and consider adoption of an ordinance amending Subchapter 35.5.7.3 of the Denton Development Code, "General Regulations", to change the Maximum Floor Area Ratio in the Industrial Center General zoning district from 0.4 to 2.0 in the City of Denton, Denton County, Texas; providing for a penalty in the maximum amount of $2,000.00 for violations thereof, severability and an effective date. (DCA14-0002, Floor Area ratio in Industrial Center General)
items.title: Public hearing: Ordinance amending Floor Area Ratio in Industrial Center General (DCA14-0002)

items.evidence_text:
95. A public hearing to receive comments to amend the City of Dallas’ Thoroughfare Plan to 
change the dimensional classifications of (1) Peterson Lane from Preston Road to 
Unnamed FN6 from a special two-lane undivided collector (SPCL 2U) roadway with 
parking within 69-feet of right-of-way and 44-feet of pavement to a special four-lane 
divided collector (SPCL 4D) roadway within 70-feet of right-of-way and 45-feet of 
pavement; (2) Peterson Lane from Unnamed FN6 to a local street Road 1 from a 
special two-lane undivided collector (SPCL 2U) roadway with parking within 69-feet of 
right-of-way and 44-feet of pavement to a special two-lane undivided (SPCL 2U) 
roadway with parking within 65-feet of right-of-way and 40-feet of pavement; and (3) 
Peterson Lane from Road 1 to Unnamed FN5 from a special two-lane undivided 
collector (SPCL 2U) roadway with parking within 69-feet of right-of-way and 44-feet of 
pavement to a special one-lane couplet (SPCL 1 CPLT) Peterson East and Peterson 
West with one-travel-lane and one-parking-lane in each direction within 38.5 feet of 
right-of-way and 26-feet of pavement; and at the close of the hearing, authorize an 
ordinance implementing the change - Financing: No cost consideration to the City
items.title: Public hearing to amend Thoroughfare Plan dimensional classifications for Peterson Lane and adopt implementing ordinance

items.evidence_text:
99. A public hearing to receive comments on a proposed municipal setting designation to 
prohibit the use of groundwater as potable water beneath property owned by Prescott 
Interests, Ltd and Prescott Interests 1300 Oak Lawn, Ltd located near the intersection of 
Oak Lawn Avenue and Market Center Boulevard and adjacent street rights-of-way; and 
an ordinance authorizing support of the issuance of a municipal setting designation to 
Prescott Interests, Ltd and Prescott Interests 1300 Oak Lawn, Ltd by the Texas 
Commission on Environmental Quality and prohibiting the use of groundwater beneath 
the designated property as potable water - Financing: No cost consideration to the City 
Recommendation of Staff: Approval
items.title: Public hearing on municipal setting designation prohibiting potable groundwater use, Prescott Interests properties, Oak Lawn Avenue and Market Center Boulevard

items.evidence_text:
100. A public hearing to receive comments on a proposed municipal setting designation to 
prohibit the use of groundwater as potable water beneath property owned by the 
Shraman South Asian Museum and Learning Center Foundation located near the 
intersection of McKinney Avenue and North Griffin Street and adjacent street rights-of-
way; and an ordinance authorizing support of the issuance of a municipal setting 
designation to the Shraman South Asian Museum and Learning Center Foundation by 
the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality and prohibiting the use of groundwater 
beneath the designated property as potable water - Financing: No cost consideration to 
the City 
Recommendation of Staff: Approval
items.title: Public hearing on municipal setting designation prohibiting potable groundwater use, Shraman South Asian Museum, McKinney Avenue and North Griffin Street

3.
Hold a discussion on complementary amendments to the Denton Development Code, specifically Subchapters 5, 7, 16, and 22, relating to Gas Well Drilling and Production, Definitions, and Procedures, in light of City Council’s action to remand DCA14-0009 back to the Planning and Zoning Commission after the Governor signed House Bill 40 into law on May 18, 2015. (Darren Groth)
items.title: Discuss complementary DDC amendments on gas well drilling/production (DCA14-0009 remand)

items.evidence_text:
1.
Consultation with Attorneys—Under Texas Government Code Section 551.071.
A.
Consult with and provide direction to City’s attorneys regarding legal issues and strategies associated with the current Gas Well Ordinance, and proposed Gas Well Ordinance amendment, regulation of gas well drilling and production within the City Limits and the extraterritorial jurisdiction, including: Constitutional limitations, statutory limitations upon municipal regulatory authority; statutory preemption and vested rights; impacts of federal and state law and regulations; impacts of gas well drilling upon protected uses and vice-versa; current and proposed extension to moratorium on drilling and production; other concerns about municipal regulatory authority or matters relating to enforcement of the Gas Well Ordinance, both current and proposed; settlement matters concerning gas well drilling in the City; surface development issues involving surface and mineral estates; and legal matters associated with a citizen’s initiative ordinance and pending litigation styled George P. Bush, Commissioner, Texas General Land Office v. City of Denton Texas, Cause No. 15-02058-362 currently pending in the 362nd District Court of Denton County and Texas Oil and Gas Association v. City of Denton, Cause No. 14-08933-431 currently pending in the 431st District Court of Denton County regarding hydraulic fracturing where a public discussion of these legal matters would conflict with the duty of the City’s attorneys under the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct of the State Bar of Texas.
items.title: Consult with City attorneys on gas well ordinance legal issues and pending litigation
